claims.text: Increasing atomic size mismatch induces greater lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys.
Greater lattice distortion enhances dislocation pinning during dynamic loading.
Enhanced dislocation pinning increases dynamic strength.
Greater lattice distortion promotes deformation twinning.
Twinning helps maintain ductility during dynamic loading.
Systematic variation of compositional ratios can produce samples spanning low to high atomic size mismatch.
Variation in atomic size mismatch produces corresponding variation in lattice distortion.
Atomic-size-induced lattice distortion creates local stress fields.
Local stress fields caused by lattice distortion act as dislocation-pinning centers under dynamic loads.
Compared with a low-distortion HEA, a high-distortion HEA will exhibit greater dynamic strength.
Compared with a low-distortion HEA, a high-distortion HEA will exhibit more pronounced strain localization.
Pronounced strain localization is indicative of dislocation pinning.
Compared with a low-distortion HEA, a high-distortion HEA will exhibit more twinning.
The proposed relationships apply to single-phase equiatomic HEAs under dynamic loading at ambient temperature.
The proposed relationships may not apply to multiphase alloys or under extreme environmental conditions.

contradictions.description: The initial state and boundary require equiatomic HEAs, but the intervention varies compositional ratios. Unless variation is restricted in a way that preserves equiatomicity, the modified samples fall outside the stated boundary.
